title: Phosphoproteomic profiling reveals reversal of dysregulated kinase signaling by nitric oxide inhibition in the Shank3 mouse model of autism.
abstract: Global proteome and phosphoproteome of cortical tissue in the Shank3 mouse model of ASD. Shank3 KO vs WT showed altered phosphorylation in synaptic, developmental and RNA-metabolism proteins. Treatment with the nNOS inhibitor 7-nitroindazole reversed phosphorylation changes in the same processes, linking nitric oxide signaling to phosphorylation. Several SFARI high-risk gene products showed altered phosphorylation reversed by NO inhibition.
methods: Proteome/phosphoproteome mass spectrometry of Shank3 KO mouse cortex +/- nNOS inhibitor; systems-biology pathway analysis.
summary: Phosphoproteomics of Shank3 KO mouse cortex shows altered phosphorylation across synaptic and RNA-metabolism proteins, partly reversed by nNOS inhibition. Touches SHANK3 (49-gene set) and SFARI high-risk genes at the protein level. Mechanism/therapeutic-target work, not variant-level; mouse model only.
